backups.title: Backups
backups.intro: The site automatically keeps copies of your work. Here you can see the copies made, make one whenever you like, and download one to your computer.
backups.reason_delai: Changes had been waiting too long (you were still working)
backups.downloadFailed: The download could not be prepared. Try again.
backups.advice: Keep a copy on your computer from time to time: backups are stored in the same place as your site. They protect you from a slip-up, not from losing the disk. Download the latest one now and then.
backups.alert: Warning: {message} It was due on {date}. Make a backup by hand (button below) and tell the person who looks after the site: the site log contains a “[backup] ALERTE” line with the details.
backups.retentionText: The last {keep}, plus the last one of each of the past {days} days (Paris time). The rest is deleted at the next backup.
backups.delayLabel: Backup even while you are working
backups.delayText: At most every {maxHours} h when changes are waiting (otherwise after {quietMin} min without changes).
backups.writing: Writing the archive: {done, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} of {total}
backups.missing: Warning: {count, plural, one {# file used by your site is not in the latest backup and cannot be recreated} other {# files used by your site are not in the latest backup and cannot be recreated}} (for example <mono>{samples}</mono>). Upload these images again (or remove them from the site); otherwise they will be broken after a restore.
backups.oldBackup: Old: without the kit drawings, imported frames or icons.
backups.unlockBody: A backup contains the whole site database. Type your password again: downloads stay unlocked for 10 minutes.
backups.includeMediaHelp: Without them, the copy is much lighter, but it only protects the text and the layout.
backups.keepHelp: The latest backups (“recent”). On top of these comes the last one of each of the past {days} days (“daily”, a server setting, BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS). The rest is deleted at the next backup. Always kept as well: the most recent one older than 48 hours and the last 3 made with “Back up now” (counted separately).
backups.quietLabel: Minutes without changes before backing up
backups.maxLabel: Maximum hours before backing up your changes, even if you are still working

blockEditors.label: Label

blockEditors.anEntryNeverExceeds: An entry never exceeds the screen height: a portrait is scaled down, not cut off.
blockEditors.fixedImagesAreCropped: Fixed: images are cropped to it (on the page, hover an image then click “Crop” to choose the area that is kept).
blockEditors.title: Title
blockEditors.eachEntryShowsA: Each entry shows a large image from the collection and leads to its page. An entry whose page is deleted or unpublished is hidden on the site.
blockEditors.aCollectionEntryShows: A collection entry shows the number of published works and, if no image is chosen, the collection's cover. “None”: a simple page, with the image you choose on the page (required).
blockEditors.tickTheProjectsIn: Tick the projects in the order you want. If you tick none, your “featured” projects are shown.
blockEditors.showsEveryProjectThat: Shows every project that has images in this collection.
blockEditors.aVideoFromYour: A video from your media library; without it, the YouTube demo reel of the Animation collection is shown. The displayed title is its alternative text.
blockEditors.theFormOpensIn: The form opens in a window (or the page scrolls to the form it contains); messages arrive in Admin → Messages. “Open the email” launches the visitor's email app.
blockEditors.aFormToWrite: A form to write to you (fields of your choice) instead of the email button. Messages arrive in Admin → Messages.
blockEditors.fixedThePortraitIs: Fixed: the portrait is cropped to it (on the page, “Crop”).
blockEditors.theSiteNameLarge: The site name, large. Remove it when the page's Opening already shows it.
blockEditors.emptyNoButtonThe: Empty: no button (the email address stays visible, as an email link).
blockEditors.projectNameAndIntroduction: Project name and introduction, at the top
blockEditors.videosFollowTheSame: Videos follow the same format as images.
blockEditors.shortFreeTextFor: Short free text, for example “2026” or “March 2026”.
blockEditors.inAGridThe: In a grid, the image fills its cell.
blockEditors.fixedTheImageIs: Fixed: the image is cropped to it (on the page, hover it then click “Crop” to choose the area that is kept).
blockEditors.withNoFixedFormat: With no fixed format, the image keeps its own. With a format: “Whole image” shows it in full (empty bands if needed), “Fill the cell” crops it. A free crop (“Crop” on the page) follows its own format.
blockEditors.aPdfOfAt: A PDF of at most 10 pages (15 MB): its pages are shown as images, and the button downloads the original PDF.
blockEditors.noExtensionLowercaseLetters: No extension: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (e.g. cv-camille-martin).
blockEditors.reuseAProjectS: Reuse a project's name and introduction
blockEditors.theTitleAndIntroduction: The title and introduction are the project's: you edit them on the page; they also change in the Projects screen and on the page, after publishing.
blockEditors.thePageSBig: The page's big title, at the top: only one per page (the home page opening already is one). A Title inserted at the top of a page with no main title becomes it right away; the others are block titles (h2).
blockEditors.computedFromThePage: Computed from the page's projects, below the title.
blockEditors.emptyInBothLanguages: Empty in both languages: no label. Empty in one language only: that language's default text.
blockEditors.emptyTheLanguageS: Empty: the language's default title (“Page not found”).
blockEditors.aSingleMessageIt: A single message: it is always shown. Several: one message is drawn at random on each visit. A message left empty in one language uses that language's default text.
blockEditors.aPublishedWorkIs: A published work is drawn at random on each visit. Never a draft, a work in the trash, or a project that no page shows.
blockEditors.shownBeforePlaybackOtherwise: Shown before playback; otherwise, the video's own image.
blockEditors.caption: Caption
blockEditors.titleBelowTheVideo: Title below the video (“Video only” presentation)
blockEditors.theAreaSHeight: The area's height follows its width. To shorten or crop it freely, drag the handles on the area's edges and corners, on the page: the images do not move. Choosing a format restores the whole area.
blockEditors.scaledKeepsTheComposition: “Scaled” keeps the composition as it is, only smaller. “Stacked” puts the images in a column, in reading order (top to bottom, then left to right).
blockEditors.yourNameAndYour: Your name and your job title are shared across the whole site (header, profile…): double-click (or double-tap) them on the page to edit them. A menu link is renamed with the “Rename” pencil that appears on it.
blockEditors.oneEntryPerCollection: One entry per collection page (page set to “This page is the collection”), in menu order: adding, removing or unpublishing a page changes the list by itself.
blockEditors.imagesFillTheCells: Images fill the cells in order; beyond that, the pattern repeats. Changing the arrangement removes nothing. Resizing a cell switches to “Custom”.
blockEditors.projectCreatedOnThis: Project created on this page: its name, context and year are edited directly on the page (double-click). It becomes public with the page.
blockEditors.imagesArePlacedMoved: Images are placed, moved and removed directly on the page. The project's name and texts are edited in the Projects screen.
blockEditors.youtubeShotFromThe: YouTube shot from the Animation collection (carried over from the old showcase). Choose a video from your media library to replace it.
blockEditors.nothingYetAddAn: Nothing yet: add an image below, or drag it from the Media tab straight onto the area.
blockEditors.givesEachCellThe: Gives each cell the shape of its image: a portrait over two rows, a panorama over two columns.
blockEditors.onThePageEach: On the page, each cell has “Alone on its row” or “With the others” in its Size menu.
blockEditors.onThePageEach2: On the page, each cell has “Wider”, “Taller”… buttons in its bar.
blockEditors.projectLimitedToThe: Project limited to the works of one discipline (carried over from an old collection page).
blockEditors.thisVideoHasSound: This video has sound: a sound button is shown, on the site as in the Preview.
blockEditors.thisFieldIsUsed: This field is used to reply to you: turn off “Used to reply to you” first.
blockEditors.youChooseTheEntries: You choose the entries, their order and their destination page.

themes.title: Themes
themes.intro: Templates never change: you have a single theme of your own, “My theme”, which you develop version after version (colours, Photoshop kit, import). Only what is online is seen by your visitors: preview, then publish.
themes.noneBody: The site is shown with the default look. The supplied themes are installed the first time a new database starts.

versions.intro: Each kit, import, template change or editing session adds a version. Going back to a version creates a new, identical one: nothing is lost. The last {count} versions are kept, along with the ones you star and the ones that have been online.

frames.title: Frames
frames.intro: Your drawn frames, to place around a photo or a video. Import as many as you like (PNG or WebP on a transparent background, or SVG), then pick one in the “Frame” menu of each image.

wallpapers.title: Wallpapers
wallpapers.intro: Your drawn patterns, to repeat as a background: across a whole page, behind a large component, or on the cards. Import as many as you like (PNG or WebP on a transparent background).

principe.title: The principle
principe.alt: Three steps: the Themes page with the download button, the kit's three Photoshop files, then the site with the drawings.
principe.b1: You download an archive with three spacious Photoshop files that contain your site as it is today.
principe.b2: You redraw whatever you like, BIG: the backdrop, the logo, the icons… The site scales it down on its own.
principe.b3: You send back the files you changed: the site takes on your style, after you approve it.

telecharger.title: Download the kit
telecharger.alt: The admin Themes page, with the “Download the Photoshop kit” button of the live theme circled.
telecharger.b1: In Themes, each theme has its own “Download the Photoshop kit” button.
telecharger.b2: You get a .zip: three .psd files and a LISEZ-MOI.txt (the readme). The kit reproduces the theme as it is saved: its layers, your logo, your drawings already applied.
telecharger.b3: A few seconds of preparation, then the archive lands in your downloads.

ouvrir.title: The three files
ouvrir.alt: The kit's three files side by side: the home backdrop in large format, the logo with the paper and the line, the icons with the cursors, the frame and the tape. Each has its instructions at the top.
ouvrir.b1: 1 · Home backdrop: one large frame, free layers. 2 · Logo and paper: what repeats or stretches. 3 · Icons and cursors: the small objects (the frame and the tape too).
ouvrir.b2: At the top of each file, a strip of instructions with an example. The cards and the _guides group are locked: don't touch them.
ouvrir.b3: You don't have to redraw everything, or send everything back: a missing file stays unchanged.

carte.title: Reading a card
carte.alt: The logo card: the large box to draw in, its caption with the displayed size, the sentence, the site thumbnail and the instructions.
carte.b1: The title gives the element and the size of its box: it is a large box, you have plenty of room.
carte.b2: The box outlined in pink is where you draw. The blue dotted lines mark the useful area.
carte.b3: Below, the size displayed on the site: the box is really scaled down (here by half).
carte.b4: The thumbnail shows in pink where it appears on your site; next to it, what is ignored and “Don't feel like it?”.

paysage.title: 1 · Home backdrop
paysage.alt: The backdrop file in the kit: the instructions strip, then the large frame; below, the home page before and after (a drawn test theme).
paysage.b1: FREE layers: each top-level layer (or group) becomes a plane. The lowest in the stack is the farthest away.
paysage.b2: You choose the number of planes (up to 8) and their order: create, delete and move layers as you like. A hidden layer is ignored.
paysage.b3: The file already contains the current backdrop, split into its planes: start from it, or start from scratch.
paysage.b4: The background plane can be opaque (a sky); keep the title area (pink frame) calm.

signature.title: 2 · Logo
signature.alt: The logo card, then the site header with the name written out, and with a drawn logo.
signature.b1: The box (2400 × 600 px) contains your name as the site writes it today.
signature.b2: Draw your logo on a transparent background. Colours kept, or a single colour tinted by the Site name: several colours are kept; a single one follows the theme.
signature.b3: The site displays it small (about 160 × 40 px to start with, adjustable with “Logo size”): keep thick strokes.
signature.b4: It replaces the name at the top left of every page.
signature.b5: Don't feel like it? Leave it as is: it is recognised and kept.

papier.title: 2 · Paper
papier.alt: The paper card with the tile and the 3 × 3 preview beside it, then a page background without and with the painted tile.
papier.b1: A 1024 × 1024 px tile, halved (512 × 512) and repeated on the background of every page.
papier.b2: Beside it, the preview of the current tile repeated 3 × 3: the pink dotted lines mark the seams.
papier.b3: No visible seam: check with Filter > Other > Offset.
papier.b4: A fine, shapeless grain: a pattern would draw a grid. Don't feel like it? Leave it as is: it is recognised and kept.

trait.title: 3 · Line
trait.alt: The line card, then the scroll bar under the boards, straight and then drawn.
trait.b1: It underlines the menu, separates the sections and serves as the bar under the boards.
trait.b2: A single colour, transparent background; 2400 × 160 px box, halved.
trait.b3: It is stretched in both directions: keep an even thickness.
trait.b4: Don't feel like it? Leave it as is: it is recognised and kept.

icones.title: Icons (file 3)
icones.alt: The icons card (four large boxes), then the “next” arrow of a board on the site (on hover): before, and after with the arrow drawn by the artist.
icones.b1: Four 512 × 512 px boxes: the arrows at the edges of the boards, the close cross of the enlarged image, the play button.
icones.b2: Draw it BIG: the site scales it down on its own, cleanly.
icones.b3: A single colour each, transparent background: the site tints them. The blue dotted lines mark the useful area.
icones.b4: Redrawing only one arrow? We offer its mirror image for the other.

curseur.title: Cursors (file 3)
curseur.alt: The cursors card in the kit, “Normal” and “Click” boxes; below, the mouse over a link on the site, system arrow then drawn cursor.
curseur.b1: Two 512 × 512 px boxes: “Normal” everywhere, “Click” on whatever can be clicked. Displayed at 32 × 32 px.
curseur.b2: The pink “hot spot” circle marks the point that clicks: move it along with your drawing.
curseur.b3: A light outline and a dark one: your mouse stays visible on every background.
curseur.b4: You can go back to the system mouse in the theme editor, without losing your drawings.

cadre.title: Frame of the collection entries (file 3)
cadre.alt: The frame card with its green lines, then the collection entries on the home page with the current mount and with a drawn frame.
cadre.b1: It surrounds the large image of each collection (Characters, Backdrops…) on the home page.
cadre.b2: Option A (recommended): draw ONE complete square frame in the 900 × 900 px box (scaled down to a third). The green lines show the cut: the corners stay as they are, the sides repeat their pattern in a loop, without being stretched, even on a panorama or a tall photo.
cadre.b3: Option B (advanced): draw only the top-left corner and the top side (orange frames) and leave the rest empty: the site rotates them to make the whole frame.
cadre.b4: When you send it, the preview shows the frame on a square, a panorama and a portrait before applying. It can also dress your photos: on a photo, choose “Theme frame” in its Frame button, or, in Themes, set “Theme frame on all photos” to Yes.
cadre.b5: Leave the centre transparent: the image shows there.
cadre.b6: Don't feel like it? Leave it as is: it is recognised and kept.

scotch.title: Tape (file 3)
scotch.alt: The tape card, then a board image without tape and with the drawn tape.
scotch.b1: The same piece is placed at the top of each board image. 1200 × 480 px box, scaled down to a third.
scotch.b2: Transparent background; partial transparency (translucent tape) is kept.
scotch.b3: Once redrawn, it turns on the “tape” variant of the boards in the new version.
scotch.b4: Don't feel like it? Leave it as is: it is recognised and kept.

regles.title: The golden rules
regles.alt: The instructions strip at the top of the backdrop file.
regles.b1: Draw BIG in the boxes: the site scales down, not you.
regles.b2: Rasterise effects, text and smart objects (Layer > Rasterise).
regles.b3: Stay in RGB 8-bit and don't resize the document.
regles.b4: Don't rename the numbered groups in files 2 and 3; you can add layers inside them. The backdrop is free.
regles.b5: Grain goes in the paper (file 2), not in the backdrop. Colours are chosen in the site editor.

renvoyer.title: Save and send back
renvoyer.alt: A theme's kit screen, with the “Send back the finished kit” area circled.
renvoyer.b1: Ctrl+S in Photoshop: PSD format, accept “Maximise compatibility”.
renvoyer.b2: In the admin, open the theme then “Send back the finished kit”: the .zip archive, a single .psd, or several .psd files chosen together.
renvoyer.b3: You can send only the files you changed; files are recognised by their content, not by their name.
renvoyer.b4: The upload resumes on its own after an interruption.

revue.title: The review screen
revue.alt: The review screen for the kit sent back by the artist: the summary, an “unchanged” card and the “Right arrow: redrawn” card with before and after.
revue.b1: The review is grouped by file; a file that was not sent is shown as “not sent: unchanged”.
revue.b2: ✓ unchanged: what you didn't touch is kept as is. ✓ redrawn: before / after, the chosen format and its weight.
revue.b3: Free backdrop: the number of planes read, and whether their composition changed.
revue.b4: ⚠ or ✗: a problem, with the reason and how to fix it in Photoshop.

appliquer.title: Apply and publish
appliquer.alt: The “Apply to my theme” panel, with the arrow mirror checkbox.
appliquer.b1: “Apply to my theme” adds a new version to My theme with your drawings (nothing is copied: no more “(kit 2)”).
appliquer.b2: You see it as a preview on your real pages, and you can always go back to the previous version.
appliquer.b3: When it's right: “Publish this version” in Themes.
appliquer.b4: The site never changes without your approval.
